sentence: This project builds a simple system that quickly shows whether tuberculosis is susceptible or resistant to certain drugs.
This project studies how motor pathways from the cerebellum and basal ganglia converge in the thalamus and how this breaks down in Parkinson's disease.
This project develops cellular immunotherapies to target melanoma and other cancers whose genetic alterations make them resist current treatments.
This project improves optical coherence tomography so it can produce high-resolution images of the tiny structures inside the human cochlea.
This project tests whether blocking a kinase in synovial fibroblasts can help treat rheumatoid arthritis, using patient tissues and a mouse model.
This project tries to find out which molecular and cellular mechanisms keep T-cell immunity against chronic viral infection working over the long term.
This project tries to reduce the cancer burden in one population through research and community engagement.
This project studies how dengue virus evolves, spreads and causes severe illness in a city, using genomic, epidemiologic, and immunologic evidence.
This project studies how cell migration shapes the surrounding environment during early human development and leads to different kinds of tissue.
This project redesigns molecules that block virus self-assembly so that cells infected with hepatitis B virus undergo programmed cell death.
This project explores what roles glycogen plays in lung cancer growth and progression to help find personalized therapies.
This project offers mass spectrometry services that measure proteins, metabolites and lipids in tissue samples for cancer research.
This project builds AI models to study Alzheimer's disease and to find cerebrospinal fluid proteins that predict cognitive decline.
This project looks for microbial and immune predictors inside tumors that show which lung cancer patients will respond to immunotherapy.
This project works to get a nanoparticle immunotherapy for lung cancer ready for manufacturing and protection of the technology.
This project studies how tumors and their surroundings cause muscle and fat loss by disrupting the metabolism of the whole body.
This project studies how cell-cell communication in the bone marrow controls blood and immune cell production and how it changes around the circadian clock.
This project tries to find out how cancer cells ignore or misinterpret signals that tell cells to stop dividing.
This project builds tools to sort out the health effects of the mixtures of chemicals that people are exposed to.
This project tries to find small molecules that block arginylation activity of arginyltransferase 1 to reduce cell death after spinal cord injury.
